item: adding a law document stores the one spelling of its jurisdiction the catalogue stores
summary: POST /api/law/documents lowercased the jurisdiction as typed and stored it, while the catalogue loader runs the field through law_jurisdiction and a restore matches law_documents rows on exact text, so a document pasted as FRA in a store that predates the country marker, or as gbr/uk anywhere, sat beside the catalogue's row under another spelling and a restore added a second row. A typed code (two or three ASCII letters) now goes through law_jurisdiction for the jurisdiction and config_country for the document's country, as the loader does; a word (france, georgia, congo) is stored as typed because the country-name index guesses. The duplicate check still finds rows an earlier version stored as typed. Stated limits: a backup written before this change can add a second row when the same alias (gb/gbr, euu, ant, uae, drc) was typed on both sides (6 pairs into an alpha-2 store, 8 into an alpha-3 store; 506 and 8 pairs improve), and rows already stored in another spelling stay as they are; the merge comparing canonical forms is proposed separately. 53 tests, 14 mutants (13 non-equivalent killed), one independent read.
